memories.content: Link each HCI research question directly to corresponding user data and analysis procedures.
In preregistered studies, specify the conditions under which deviations from the plan are permissible.
In preregistered studies, specify how to record content that deviates from the plan.
Commit to one exact target number of participants so the schedule, workload, and budget can be checked against the same quantity.
Specify the interview protocols, recording devices, or log tools used to collect each type of user data.
Specify whether each type of user data is collected before, during, or after the interaction.
Readers cannot tell whether the schedule and budget agree when different sections imply different target counts.
In formative evaluation prototypes, implementation instability exists as an independent cause of task failure alongside design choices.
If a prototype safety signal occurs during formative evaluation, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over planned data collection.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to the data and analysis.
The author of this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Calculate the required sessions, facilitator hours, and participant payments from the same exact target rather than from separate rough estimates.
If recruitment falls below the exact target, state the shortfall explicitly and revise the affected schedule or deliverable.
Do not use a wide range merely to postpone choosing the quantity that the rest of the proposal must support.
Specify in one sentence the user population and actual usage environment to which the design knowledge applies.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through the specified target population and environment.
Specify the workflow, technical infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions that must match before applying the design guidelines at another field site.
The transferability of field design knowledge depends not only on user characteristics but also on workflow and technological–organizational infrastructure.
The user tends to apply results confirmed at one deployment site to all similar organizations.

analysis.overview: The reference frame concentrates on research answerability, preregistration, data collection, participant-count consistency, prototype risk, and proposal-writing habits. The compared frame independently addresses the boundaries and transfer conditions of field-design knowledge, including a tendency to overgeneralize from one site.

relations.reason: The reference memories state the same one-sided traceability principle as an authoring requirement and a reviewer criterion.
relations.summary: Research answerability requires a traceable path from each question to its user data and analysis.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame supplies this policy for conditions authorizing preregistration deviations.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should define when departures from the plan are permitted.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame supplies this documentation requirement for deviating content.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should define how departures from the plan are recorded.

relations.reason: The reference memories jointly state and motivate one underlying planning rule: avoid ranges or inconsistent estimates and derive operational commitments from the same exact target.
relations.summary: A proposal should use one exact participant target consistently across scheduling, workload, sessions, staffing, payments, and budget.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame specifies the instruments and procedures used to collect user data.
relations.summary: Each user-data type should identify its collection protocol, recording device, or logging tool.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame specifies the temporal placement of user-data collection.
relations.summary: Each user-data type should identify whether collection occurs before, during, or after interaction.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame distinguishes implementation instability from design choices when interpreting failures.
relations.summary: In formative prototype evaluation, implementation instability is an independent possible cause of task failure.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame establishes this conditional safety priority.
relations.summary: A formative-evaluation safety signal makes institutional safety procedures take precedence over planned data collection.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame records this proposal-writing tendency.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame specifies the response to a participant shortfall.
relations.summary: Recruitment below the exact target should be disclosed and reflected in affected schedules or deliverables.

relations.reason: The compared memories express the same one-sided boundary principle as an authoring instruction and a reviewer criterion.
relations.summary: The applicable generalization boundary should be stated through the target user population and actual usage environment.

relations.reason: The compared memories jointly describe the contextual conditions governing transfer to another field site.
relations.summary: Transferring field-design guidance requires matching workflow, technical infrastructure, and organizational or operational-authority conditions, not merely user characteristics.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame records this behavioral tendency toward site-to-organization overgeneralization.
relations.summary: The user tends to generalize findings from one deployment site to all similar organizations.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only guidance defines population, environment, workflow, infrastructure, and authority boundaries for transfer, while noting overgeneralization from individual deployments.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only guidance covers traceable research questions, preregistration deviations, collection methods and timing, exact recruitment planning, prototype failure and safety, and feature-list framing.
